notes.title: 🌱 Release notes 1.0.10
notes.notes:
Release Highlights

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45335281/51d916fd92870de25ade44ffca512f878835c821.png"]

🦖 Features
Added support for Chinese localization (Simplified and Traditional). The app will automatically match your system’s preferred language, and fall back to English if a translation isn’t available.


🐞 Bug fixes & improvements
Fixed scroll bar style in benchmark selection menu.

Fixed an issue that could cause a crash when running a Ray Tracing benchmark.

Fixed incorrect app icon on certain Android devices.

Improved clarity around which Evolve edition (Free, Advanced, or Professional) a user is running.

Evolve Advanced: The current loop index is now displayed during benchmark runs when using the --loop command-line option.

notes.title: 🐊 Release notes 1.0.9
notes.notes:
Release Highlights


[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45335281/10e7dc715c0c80d3d13d55477cfa99b0dcc98af1.png"]


🦖 Features


Acceleration Structure Compaction

Our ray tracing system now supports acceleration structure compaction, a feature designed to reduce memory usage. After an acceleration structure is built, the system can optimize it to occupy less GPU memory while maintaining the same rendering quality and performance.

This means more efficient use of graphics resources, leaving additional memory available for textures, larger scenes, and richer visual effects. With compaction, you get the same ray tracing results at a lower memory cost, enabling better scalability and smoother performance across a wide range of hardware.

As part of evolutionary benchmarking, we’ll continue updating Evolve with the latest techniques. As such, acceleration structure compaction is now enabled by default. This will slightly affect your acceleration structure build score.


✍️ Additional Information

notes.title: 🌿 Release notes 1.0.7
notes.notes:
Release Highlights

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45335281/79cd6176e48c71b7d14ee7e61dfb85ba3c9eb687.png"]

🐞 Bug fixes & improvements
Fixed an issue where exiting a fullscreen benchmark early using Esc did not return the application to windowed mode.

Fixed an issue where the Hall of Fame page displayed obfuscated email addresses instead of usernames.

Fixed an issue where command-line runs required authentication via the start menu. These now use browser-based authentication.

Fixed an issue where certain workloads were not properly included in the ray tracing score calculation when performing a pipeline raytracing benchmark. As a result of this correction, the ray tracing score may now be slightly lower going forward.

Fixed various issues affecting highscore server stability.

Increased the minimum required NVIDIA driver version to 576.80.

The window title now reflects the presence of the Advanced DLC.


🧜‍♂️ Thank you!

A big shoutout to Server075, MMR, Greebo-t-c, and saltycroissant for your invaluable support — from reporting bugs and providing detailed follow-ups to actively running our software. Your contributions have been a huge help in making Evolve better!

notes.title: 🦖 Release notes 1.0.4
notes.notes:
Release Highlights


[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45335281/4bf8ed87f824ee216f83f036ed5da002d0426a00.png"]


🦖 Features

Evolve Advanced: Save and upload benchmark results
Evolve Advanced users can now save benchmark results to disk and upload them at a later time, offering enhanced flexibility and control over your benchmarking workflow.



Saving benchmark results:

To save your benchmark results, use the --result command-line argument during a benchmark run:
[code]./evolve.exe --result path/to/result[/code]
When the benchmark completes, the results are stored locally as a .evolve file at the specified location.

Note: Saving results to disk disables automatic benchmark submission.



Uploading saved results:

To upload your saved .evolve benchmark results, use the Evolve Offline Submit tool (evolve-offline-submit.exe), included with your Evolve installation.
[olist]
Navigate to your Evolve install directory.

Open a command shell.

Run the following command:
[/olist][code]./evolve-offline-submit.exe path/to/result.evolve[/code]
If the upload is successful, you will receive a link to your uploaded results, making it easy to access and share.


Evolve Advanced: Offline mode
Evolve Advanced users can now run Evolve in offline mode, allowing you to skip authentication and benchmark submissions entirely. This provides greater flexibility for isolated environments or private benchmarking sessions.

To launch Evolve in offline mode, use the --offline command-line argument:
[code]./evolve.exe --offline[/code]

🐞 Bug fixes & improvements
The benchmark settings menu now shows the selected benchmark mode.

On desktop, improved alignment of score dials in the benchmark results menu.

On desktop, improved graph’s “on hover” tool tip visibility.

Improved stability on Adreno 830 devices. These include the Samsung Galaxy S25 series, Xiaomi 15 series, OnePlus 13 series, and more.


🧜‍♂️ Thank you!
Thanks Albrecht Mesotten from HwBot for the save and upload feature request!

Thanks Harish Jonnalagadda from Android Central for the Adreno 830 stability report.

Release Highlights
 [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45335281/87391b91c31e5fdd68e04e2411d4145fd6e3b378.png"]


🕺Announcements
Make sure to check out our technical guide for more information on exactly what the scores mean, and on how to set up a repeatable benchmark.


🦖 Features
New hall of fame page on the evolve website! See https://www.evolvebenchmark.com/hall-of-fame

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45335281/b54a5ac26853faedd645cf5d548519d2a468e711.png"][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45335281/9218422608fde41fabcd19a658d183d05c2f85ec.png"]
🐞 Bug fixes & improvements
Temporarily disable benchmark interrupts for the Intel driver-configured frame limiter. This was incorrectly giving false positives due to a bug in the intel driver control library, resulting in a benchmark always being interrupted on Intel devices that had this feature set. The bug has been reported to Intel.

Fixes the social media sharing buttons moving outside the results screen for a window that uses letter-boxing.

Resolved an issue with authentication which could lead to users having to re authenticate when it wasn’t necessary.


🧜‍♂️ Thank you!
Thanks Pieter Plaisier from skatterbencher.com for reporting the frame limiter issue on Intel!

notes.title: 🦕 Release notes 1.0.1
notes.notes:
Release Highlights


[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45335281/8d49d9310a7495ac4dedbef36504e5f9ed1f1ec6.png"]


🕺Announcements
 Thanks for being some of our first users to download and play around with Evolve!

 This release going forward requires the use of NVIDIA 565 drivers or higher


🐞 Bug fixes & improvements
 On NVIDIA we now report fan speed in RPM rather then as a percentage. Previously we were using an API that would report fan speed as a percentage which would occasionally go over 100% leading to confusion with some of our users.

 On Intel we now collect fan speed in RPM

 On Intel we collect total board power usage (in Watt).

 Crisper UI rendering due to improved anti-aliasing and blending. We were previously interpolating the UI colors in an incorrect color space, leading to incorrect results.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45335281/7fe8f9e05d20eb325aa14b498fc6a42bdbd04051.png"]

Before, image has sharp and pixelated lines

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45335281/70ea0b9b5d5ca98901e290dd405781a3c861a12c.png"]

After, image has smooth and nicely anti-aliased lines


🧜‍♂️ Thank you!
Thanks Potato Head and Albuquerque from the Beyond3D forums for reporting the odd fan speed behavior on NVIDIA!
